originality.rationale: The claim is the constrained phase-only sharp visible-space conditioning law over all finite abelian groups, with optimizers depending on exponent. Generic Weyl eigenvalue identities and cyclic rank discriminants are excluded from the novelty claim. Closest accessible abstracts do not imply noncyclic exponent optimization or unit-circle stability optimum, though full inspection of two cyclic research records was blocked and an equivalent hidden theorem remains a material risk.
residual_risks: The cyclic-only rank-discriminant and impulse-conditioning complete research files were not accessible; indexed abstracts do not rule out a phase-only special-case computation in their proofs.
Unidentified older quantum measurement literature might independently solve the constrained phase-spacing problem.
General Weyl machinery is prior mathematics; novelty lies only in constrained exact exponent law and phase optimizer classification.

value.rationale: This solves a natural minimally modified phase-only design problem with an exact rank capacity theorem and sharp stability cost. The condition number varies sharply at fixed order N with group exponent (e.g., the three abelian groups of order eight). The quantitative bound tells how much robustness a one-defect constant-amplitude design can attain before introducing additional phase controls, rather than being just a numerical instance or renaming of rank discrimination.
